page: Google Cloud Platform m2-ultramem-416 is an x86_64 architecture memory-optimized server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon processors. It features 416 vCPUs, consisting of 208 physical cores with hyper-threading, operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 11.50 TB of RAM, yielding an allocation of 28.31 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between single-core and multi-core performance. While single-core metrics are weak, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores, the massive core count delivers top-tier multi-core performance. Stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU tests rank in the top tier. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with cached read speeds reaching 20,571.16 GB/sec and uncached write speeds at 296.37 GB/sec. Redis SET operations also perform in the top tier, achieving 324.46 million operations per second, alongside high static web serving throughput.

This server represents a high-density hardware profile designed for enterprise workloads where memory capacity is the primary constraint. Given the absence of local storage and GPUs, its qualitative cost efficiency is optimized for memory-bound, in-memory database operations and large-scale data processing rather than general-purpose compute or graphics-intensive tasks. It is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, and massive memory-bound data analytics.
